summary: Iteration 6 backend-only bug-fix verification for 'user-created merchant lost on signout + force reseed'. Created /app/backend/tests/test_signout_reseed_persistence.py with a full 10-step E2E scenario + two regression assertions (exact counts + no accumulation across repeated reseeds). All 3 new tests PASS (3/3). Ran the requested regression suites — Phase 2 merchant + loyalty (25 tests) and iter5 reset-password + category filter (8 tests) + iter4 merchant flow (9 tests): 42/42 PASS. Combined iteration 6 result: 45/45 backend tests green. The fix in _do_seed() correctly (a) only deletes demo docs where owner_id == None, (b) only deletes deals whose merchant_id is in the demo-merchant set, (c) preserves user merchants + user deals across arbitrary numbers of force reseeds (verified with 3 back-to-back reseeds — demo merchant count stays at exactly 6, user merchant survives). After reseed, /merchant/me returns the same profile, /merchant/deals returns the user's deal, and /api/deals?category=cafe returns BOTH the user's cafe deal AND the freshly regenerated demo cafe deals from Brew House Coffee. Post-reseed the user is able to re-login with the same email/password and the JWT still resolves to a merchant role. No regressions detected in Phase 2, iter4, or iter5 suites.

minor.issue: The endpoint is unauthenticated and force=true is publicly callable — anyone can trigger a demo re-seed (which is what the city-switcher relies on). Not a data-loss issue anymore after the fix, but consider gating with a shared token or rate-limiting so an attacker can't hammer it. Flagged for hardening, not blocking.

action_items: (Optional hardening) Gate POST /api/seed?force=true behind an internal token or short-lived per-IP rate limit — currently anyone can trigger a demo reseed by hitting the public URL.

(Optional) The old /app/backend/tests/test_happyhour_api.py still has 4 pre-existing failing assertions that assume static seed counts and were flagged in iteration 5. Not iter6 regressions, but recommend deleting or rewriting to be count-tolerant when convenient.
critical_code_review_comments: _do_seed() force branch now correctly scopes deletes: db.merchants.delete_many({owner_id: None}) and db.deals.delete_many({merchant_id: {$in: demo_ids}}). Confirmed by test that user merchants with owner_id set AND their deals (which carry that merchant_id but were NOT in demo_ids) both survive reseed.
Defensive insert_many guards (if merchants / if all_deals) prevent BulkWriteError on empty arrays — good.

Deals belonging to the user merchant are matched by merchant_id (not owner_id) for deletion, which is the correct approach: even if a user's deal had a NULL owner_id (edge case), it would still be preserved because its merchant_id is not in the demo set.

One theoretical edge: if a user creates a deal against a demo merchant's id (impossible via /merchant/deals since that endpoint always ties to the caller's merchant, but possible if someone injects), it would still be deleted. Not exploitable via public API surface today.
SIGNOUT itself was never the culprit — login/logout is stateless JWT with no server call. The report's RCA is accurate: the destructive path was force-reseed, and it is now surgically scoped.

success_rate.backend: 100% — 3/3 new persistence tests + 25/25 Phase 2 + 8/8 iter5 + 9/9 iter4 = 45/45 pass on iteration-6 scope.

seed_data_creation: Each test-run creates one ephemeral user (email prefix 'iter6_' + uuid) and one user-owned merchant (name 'Iter6 Persist Cafe <hex>') + one cafe deal. These accumulate in the DB (no server-side test teardown) but do not affect assertions because the tests key off exact ids the test itself created. Demo data is fully reset each test via force reseed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 6 fix verified: user merchants + deals survive force reseed. Full E2E is covered by /app/backend/tests/test_signout_reseed_persistence.py::TestMerchantSurvivesForceReseed::test_full_e2e_persistence. For future runs, keep this + the iter5 (reset-password/category) + Phase 2 + iter4 suites in the regression pipeline. Base URL comes from /app/frontend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. If iter6 test file is run in isolation, env var is auto-loaded from /app/frontend/.env by the module-level shim.
rca_of_issue: RCA: Original _do_seed(force=True) called db.merchants.delete_many({}) and db.deals.delete_many({}), unconditionally wiping ALL merchants and ALL deals. The customer 'Change city' UI in /frontend calls POST /api/seed?force=true anonymously, so any city-switch would nuke every user-created merchant. Signout itself was never destructive (JWT client-only), but users perceived data loss after logout because the very next city switch (or admin action) wiped everything. FIX: filter delete_many to owner_id == None and scope the deals delete to merchant_ids of those demo merchants. VERIFICATION: E2E test creates a merchant + deal, force-reseeds with different lat/lng, re-logs in, and asserts merchant + deal still queryable. Also verified 3 repeated reseeds keep demo merchant count at exactly 6 (no duplication). REPRODUCTION (pre-fix): 1) register user, 2) onboard merchant, 3) POST /api/seed?force=true, 4) GET /api/merchant/me → 404. Post-fix: same flow returns 200 with the original merchant.
